definitions.explanation: A type of grasshopper found in rice paddies and fields throughout Japan. Historically an agricultural pest that damaged rice crops, but also traditionally eaten as food in certain regions.

examples.japanese: ⟦{田|た}んぼ→田んぼ：00402_tanbo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧イナゴ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: There were lots of rice grasshoppers in the rice paddy.

examples.japanese: イナゴ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{佃煮|つくだに}→佃煮：04970_tsukudani⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{長野県|ながのけん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{名物|めいぶつ}→名物：05591_meibutsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Rice grasshoppers simmered in soy sauce are a specialty of Nagano Prefecture.

examples.japanese: イナゴ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{大量発生|たいりょうはっせい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{農作物|のうさくぶつ}→農作物：15271_nousakubutsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{深刻|しんこく}→深刻：01567_shinkoku⟧な⟦{被害|ひがい}→被害：02572_higai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: A large outbreak of rice grasshoppers can cause serious damage to agricultural crops.

notes:
Usually written in katakana as イナゴ when referring to the creature (standard for animal/insect names in Japanese). The kanji {稲子|いなご} or {蝗|いなご} exists but is rarely used in modern writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- イナゴ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{佃煮|つくだに}→佃煮：04970_tsukudani⟧ — locusts simmered in sweetened soy sauce (a traditional preserved food)
- イナゴ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{大量発生|たいりょうはっせい} — locust outbreak / locust plague
- イナゴ{捕|と}り — catching locusts (a rural activity, once common for children)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦バッタ→バッタ：06515_batta⟧ — grasshopper (broader category; イナゴ is a specific type of ⟦バッタ→バッタ：06515_batta⟧)
- {蝗害|こうがい} — locust plague (damage from locust swarms)
- ⟦{害虫|がいちゅう}→害虫：06430_gaichuu⟧ — harmful insect; pest

CULTURAL NOTE:
Eating insects ({昆虫食|こんちゅうしょく}) has a long history in certain regions of Japan, particularly in mountainous areas like {長野県|ながのけん} and {群馬県|ぐんまけん}. イナゴ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{佃煮|つくだに}→佃煮：04970_tsukudani⟧ (locusts simmered in soy sauce and sugar) is the most well-known example and is still sold commercially today. In recent years, insect eating has attracted renewed interest as a sustainable protein source.
